topic: Why the stock market just crashed

beats.text: In one morning, more than $2 trillion vanished from the S&P 500 – here’s why the market tumbled on November 5, 2026, and whether the AI bubble finally popped.
The Top
AI stocks carried the market like a single massive weight. Nvidia alone was worth $5.4 trillion, roughly eight cents of every dollar in the S&P.
The four biggest cloud companies plan to spend over $700 billion this year building data centers, more than $1 trillion next year.
beats.label: Cloud-capex

beats.text: It felt like a single horse pulling the whole carriage.

dialogue.speaker: THE TRADER
dialogue.line: It felt like a single horse pulling the whole carriage.

beats.text: How the AI hype built the market tower:
lines: Investors poured money into AI and chip stocks.
Corporate spending plans ballooned to $700 billion for data centers.
The market became a house of cards.

beats.text: We’re building data-center capacity faster than anyone can pay for it.

dialogue.speaker: THE DEVELOPER
dialogue.line: We’re building data-center capacity faster than anyone can pay for it.

beats.text: The Cracks
Nvidia was owed $63 billion for chips shipped but not paid for. CoreWeave owed over $5 for every $1 of equity.
Nvidia took a $400 million hit on unsold H200 chips stuck in Hong Kong.
beats.label: H200 loss

beats.text: We ordered chips we could never serve.

dialogue.speaker: THE INVESTOR
dialogue.line: We ordered chips we could never serve.

beats.text: Microsoft trimmed its spending plan from $175 billion to $170 billion, a cut of less than 3 percent, just a week before the crash.
The Rally
Wednesday the Dow surged 1,569 points, about a 3 percent jump, the best post-midterm day since 1982.
beats.label: Wednesday rally

beats.text: Democrats won the House and Senate, but voters in 10 states rejected data-center subsidies, dampening optimism even as oil fell more than 9 percent.
We were riding a wave of cheap energy.

dialogue.speaker: THE ENERGY ANALYST
dialogue.line: We were riding a wave of cheap energy.

beats.text: The Morning
The day in minutes:
ticks: 9:30 AM – The bell rings, futures tumble.
9:31 AM – S&P opens flat, Nvidia already slipping.
9:45 AM – Cloud-capex data released, investors stare.
10:35 AM – Nasdaq down 4 percent, Dow down 700 points.
11:17 AM – VIX up 65 percent, fear spikes.
11:30 AM – Nvidia drops 9 percent, loses $400 billion.

beats.text: Across the S&P more than $2 trillion evaporated by mid-morning.
beats.label: Market melt

beats.text: It was like watching a sandcastle wash away.

dialogue.speaker: THE TRADER
dialogue.line: It was like watching a sandcastle wash away.

beats.text: Who Gets Hurt
Small investors sold a net $358 million of stock, the most since March 2020.
beats.label: Retail sell-off

beats.text: About 70 million Americans hold 401(k) accounts, most in index funds. Their balances took a hit as the market fell.
My retirement feels a step back.

dialogue.speaker: THE SAVER
dialogue.line: My retirement feels a step back.

beats.text: Northern Virginia data-center hookups now wait about seven years, adding $25-30 to monthly bills for households.
A small-business owner in Ohio says credit dried up after the crash, forcing a postponement of a planned expansion.
A college student in Texas watches his internship stipend evaporate as the market tanks, worrying about tuition payments.
Did It Pop?
The 47 biggest AI and chip stocks lost about $5 trillion in the month before the crash.
beats.label: AI wipe-out

beats.text: The dot-com crash took two and a half years to erase a similar amount. This AI decline happened in four weeks.
Four weeks to melt five trillion.

dialogue.speaker: THE ECONOMIST
dialogue.line: Four weeks to melt five trillion.

beats.text: Why the AI bubble popped:
lines: Revenue growth slowed as chip orders stalled.
Unpaid invoices piled up, creating cash crunches.
Spending plans for data centers faced political roadblocks.
Investors rushed to sell, amplifying the fall.

beats.text: The Aftermath
At a kitchen table, a retiree checks a 401(k) statement and sees the red numbers. The electric bill glows higher, a reminder of data-center costs.
When the AI hype fades, the ordinary investor feels the echo — will the next wave lift or crush again?
